parts.text:
Regenerate the GeminiSupervisor truth-reading implementation and related Supervisor integration using the following latest design as authoritative, while preserving all still-applicable existing runtime/dependency behavior. Return COMPLETE replacement/new repository files, not patches or excerpts.

1. PRESERVE CURRENT CANONICAL/READER CONTRACT. Keep ChatMachines/GeminiSupervisor/dependency-map.json as the authoritative registry and preserve its existing version/description/sentinel_file/mappings semantics. Do not replace or simplify the existing mappings object. Preserve the deterministic stable-reader mechanism and per-document provenance: canonical_path, stable_reader_path, source_blob_sha, source_commit_sha, reader_blob_sha, item_count, last_synced_at. Stable readers remain deterministic ordered JSON projections mechanically derived from canonical files and are regenerated only when their own canonical source changes. Canonical files do NOT need to have the same representation as their projections.

2. REMOVE THE SEED/PROOF SWAP PUZZLE. The new reading proof is deterministic repair of a randomly damaged copy of the projection. The stable projection itself is the trusted answer key and normalized reading surface. There are no truth seeds, proof values, submitted-seed arrays, gap IDs, or per-gap bookkeeping.

3. NONCE-SCOPED CHALLENGES. Each Supervisor run_nonce gets an isolated truth-reader area under ChatMachines/GeminiSupervisor/runs/<run_nonce>/truth-reader/ (or an equivalently clear run-scoped structure). Global stable readers remain shared/read-only. Each nonce-scoped document challenge must include BOTH: (a) an intact full projection copied from the current stable reader, and (b) a repair projection produced from that same full projection by randomized damage. The projection metadata must bind the challenge to the run_nonce and document/provenance so a repaired challenge cannot be transplanted between runs. Multiple Supervisor runs must not collide.

4. FULL PROJECTION + DAMAGED REPAIR COPY. The worker is explicitly given the full nonce-scoped projection to read/compare and the damaged repair projection to edit. The instruction is simply to completely restore the repair projection until it exactly matches the full projection, changing nothing else. This intentionally proves acquisition/use of the supplied full projection; it is not necessary to force retrieval from the canonical native-format source directly. Provenance establishes what the projection represents.

5. RANDOM, DISTRIBUTED DAMAGE. Damage approximately 10% of eligible projection content using crypto-secure randomness. Removals must be spread across the whole document rather than allowed to cluster: divide the eligible ordered projection into multiple regions/bands and make randomized selections within each sufficiently large region. Do not use a deterministic every-Nth pattern. Avoid selecting only trivial/null/empty values when substantial values are available. For JSON/object-like projection units, prefer removal of complete key/value pairs; for array-like ordered content, remove complete elements/records. The exact representation may remain the current stable-reader representation, but damage must preserve a syntactically valid JSON challenge.

6. GENERIC PLACEHOLDERS ONLY. Every removed key/value pair or removed unit should use the same generic placeholder concept, such as '^MISSING_KEY^': '^MISSING_VALUE^'. Do NOT itemize gaps, number them, assign gap IDs, expose original positions beyond what is naturally necessary to keep the damaged projection usable, or maintain a worker-visible answer map. The test is complete repair, so individual gap identities are unnecessary. If repeated identical JSON object keys would make one object syntactically/semantically impossible, structure the projection/damage representation so repeated generic placeholder records remain valid while still using the same generic placeholder values for all removals.

7. PASS CONDITION. Deterministic verification compares the worker-edited repair projection against the intact nonce-scoped full projection using exact structural/deep equality. PASS requires the repaired projection to equal the full projection completely and contain no missing placeholders. Gemini must not decide repair correctness, provenance correctness, damage selection, or truth PASS.

8. FAIL/PASS LIFECYCLE. On FAIL, restore the exact original damaged repair projection for that same nonce/document so the identical challenge can be retried; do not advance or silently create a new damaged challenge. On PASS, remove transient active/damaged challenge material as appropriate but retain a compact durable PASS verification record under that run_nonce so the Supervisor can later prove that exact run passed its reading gate. Do not delete another run's state. Workflow-generated commits must not recursively retrigger.

9. SUPERVISOR INTEGRATION / GENERATED FORMS. Incorporate the agreed direction that Step 0 should be system-generated as a deterministic form rather than requiring the worker to manufacture its return schema from scratch. Prepopulate and lock fields already known by the system (including run_nonce, verbatim user request, step number, required role, generation timestamp, and the authoritative selectable document universe). Expose explicit worker-fillable requirement fields and document-selection booleans. Selected required documents should drive creation of that same run_nonce's truth-reader full+repair projections. Design this so the same form pattern can later extend to Steps 1-4 without requiring that all later steps be converted in this revision unless needed for consistency. Preserve existing Supervisor state-machine semantics and Gemini supervisory gates; do not replace semantic evaluation with the form mechanism.

10. WORKFLOW/FILE INTEGRATION. Update the actual active implementation paths, including scripts/workflows/control surfaces, not merely a design proposal. Preserve the existing GeminiSupervisor dependency alignment workflow and sentinel behavior. Update README documentation to describe the deployed truth-reader verification lifecycle, nonce scoping, stable-reader provenance, full-vs-repair comparison, random distributed damage, generic placeholders, PASS/FAIL behavior, and Step 0 generated-form integration. If files introduced by the old global seed/proof implementation are obsolete, explicitly return DELETE actions for them or complete replacements that migrate them to the nonce-scoped repair model.

Return response_type='truth_reader_repair_and_forms_implementation' with files[] entries containing: path, action ('CREATE'|'REPLACE'|'DELETE'), purpose, and complete_content (null only for DELETE). Include every file required to install the design safely, especially dependency-map.json if modified, stable-reader sync helper if modified, truth challenge/repair engine, truth challenge workflow, Supervisor runtime/config/Agents.md changes required for Step 0 generated forms and nonce coupling, README.md, and any new run-scoped form/challenge helper/template files. Do not return synthetic abbreviated files or placeholders.
